title: Tom Brahaney: Two-Time Consensus All-American Center
question: Which Oklahoma center was a consensus All-American in 1971 and 1972 and later a College Football Hall of Famer?
answer: Tom Brahaney, who played at Oklahoma from 1970 to 1972, was a consensus All-America center in both 1971 and 1972. The College Football Hall of Fame inducted him in 2007.
summary: Tom Brahaney anchored OU's Wishbone line, faced Rich Glover in the 1971 Game of the Century, and became a two-time consensus All-American and Hall of Famer.
body: Tom Brahaney grew up in Midland, Texas, and played at Oklahoma from 1970 through 1972. The College Football Hall of Fame notes that he became a starter about halfway through his sophomore season, a year before the Sooners installed the Wishbone offense.

The Wishbone fit a center who could block with precision. Oklahoma led the nation in rushing, total offense and scoring while Brahaney was the starting center, and the Hall of Fame says he consistently graded in the 90s on his blocking assignments.

In 1971 he earned all-conference and consensus All-America honors. The Sooners went 11-1 and finished No. 2 in the final polls, and Brahaney drew one of the most-watched matchups in the Game of the Century against Nebraska, lining up against future Hall of Famer Rich Glover. Nebraska won that game 35-31.
He returned as a senior captain in 1972, was a Lombardi Award finalist, and was again a consensus All-American, making him a two-time selection.

St. Louis picked him in the fifth round of the 1973 NFL Draft, and he spent nine seasons with the Cardinals, from 1973 through 1981. The College Football Hall of Fame welcomed him into its 2007 class.
